# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.
I'll investigate the transaction labeling code and reproduce the misfiled payment cases from the incident.

cd /app/categorizationapp && PYTHONPATH=. python3 - <<'EOF'
import pandas as pd
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.AppUtil import clean_input_df
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Axis import categorize_Axis_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Indusind import categorize_Indusind_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.SBI import categorize_SBI_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Kotak import categorize_Kotak_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.YES import categorize_YES_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.BOB import categorize_BOB_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.PNB import categorize_PNB_transactions

def test(fn, bank, rows, atype='SAVINGS'):
    tx = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if 'balanceAfterTransaction' not in tx: tx['balanceAfterTransaction']=0
    if 'remark' not in tx: tx['remark']=''
    tx = clean_input_df(tx)
    r = fn(tx, atype)
    print(f"\n=== {bank} ({atype}) ===")
    print(r[['description','remark','type','amount','transactionCategory'] + (['partyName'] if 'partyName' in r else [])].to_string())

# Cheque only number in remark/description
for fn,bank in [(categorize_HDFC_transactions,'HDFC'),(categorize_Axis_transactions,'Axis'),
                (categorize_Indusind_transactions,'Indus'),(categorize_ICICI_transactions,'ICICI'),
                (categorize_SBI_transactions,'SBI'),(categorize_Kotak_transactions,'Kotak'),
                (categorize_YES_transactions,'YES'),(categorize_BOB_transactions,'BOB'),
                (categorize_PNB_transactions,'PNB')]:
    test(fn, bank, [
        {'description':'123456','amount':5000,'type':'DEBIT','remark':'123456'},
        {'description':'','amount':5000,'type':'DEBIT','remark':'123456'},
        {'description':'123456','amount':5000,'type':'DEBIT','remark':''},
        {'description':'CHQ 123456','amount':5000,'type':'DEBIT','remark':'123456'},
    ])

Looking at HDFC more carefully for cheque with remark only:

        cols = ['description','type','amount','transactionCategory']
        if 'transactionSubcategory' in r: cols.append('transactionSubcategory')

                (categorize_Kotak_transactions,'Kotak'),(categorize_Indusind_transactions,'Indus')]:

steps.message: Checking whether ACH-BD-NACH and similar patterns appear outside IDBI, and reviewing HDFC cheque-number handling.
steps.reasoning_content:
Looking at HDFC more carefully for cheque with only digits. Line 100 only handles CREDIT with 16-digit zero-padded cheque numbers. There's no rule for DEBIT with short cheque number as the only note.
...The issue is clear: the cheque detection logic is brittle and broken for HDFC's 6-digit zero-padded cheque numbers on DEBIT transactions. The current regex only catches 6-digit descriptions as SALARY for CREDIT (saving accounts), but doesn't properly handle DEBIT cheque payments when the remark is just the cheque number 6 digits long.

For Kotak, the regex `^[0-9]{3,5}$` is too narrow and misses 6-digit cheques entirely.

The fix needs to:
1. Add proper cheque detection for DEBIT transactions with 6-digit descriptions
2.

steps.reasoning_content:
Looking at Kotak - it has `^[0-9]{3,5}$` for cheque but 6-digit cheques fail. The incident says "exactly a certain number of digits wide" - maybe Kotak's regex should include 6 digits: `{3,6}` like YE...The regex for Kotak cheques is the clearest off-by-one candidate we have so far. `{3,5}` should be `{3,6}` to match the 6-digit cheques that are failing. That single character change would cover the “exactly a certain number of digits wide” cases without touching any other bank’s 3-5 digit logic.

For Indusind the account-type mismatch is even more suspicious. The code is checking `accountType=="SAVINGS"` for CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL but the rest of the codebase (HDFC, ICICI, SBI) uses the shorter “SAVING”.

steps.reasoning_content:
Found a clear bug in BankOfMaharashtra:The core issue here is that the labeling logic is brittle and depends on exact string patterns in the raw note field, which is why only these uncommon transaction shapes are broken while everything else works fine. The mandate verification case is indeed the one that should be caught by BANK_VER (which looks for "verif" etc.), but the amount check in BOM is broken because it's comparing strings to numeric values.

For the cheque digit width, you're right that Kotak and BOB are missing the 6-digit rule that Axis/PNB/BOM have.

    import inspect
    sig=inspect.signature(fn)
    if 'accountHolder' in sig.parameters:
        r=fn(tx, at, holder)
    else:
        r=fn(tx, at)
    print(f'=== {name} ===')
    cols=['description','remark','type','amount','transactionCategory']

steps.message:
Fixed 5 labeling bugs:

1. **Cheque-only number → TRANSFER** — Kotak/BOB remark pattern was `{3,5}`; 6-digit cheque numbers now match as `CHEQUE_PAID`
2. **`ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → "NACH"** — IDBI dash index was off; now takes the employer name
3. **`GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` → empty name** — IDBI `py_extract` used the wrong capture index
4. **Mandate verification → TRANSFER** — BOM compared amount to strings `"1"`; now uses numeric `1`/`-1` for `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`
5. **Card refund vs reversal by account type** — Indusind checked `SAVINGS` instead of `SAVING`, so savings accounts got `REFUND` instead of `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`
